records.summary: Snow outlines the branching channels at the mouth of the Mississippi. Here the river divides as it carries water and sediment out to sea.

records.title: Inside an Elodea leaf
records.summary: The green bodies inside these leaf cells are chloroplasts. Within them, the plant uses light energy to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water.

records.caption: The green bodies inside these leaf cells are chloroplasts. Within them, the plant uses light energy to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water.

records.derivative: Uncropped archive JPEG, maximum edge 1800 pixels.

records.caption: A boulder coral called Big Momma rises above the reef in American Samoa. The colony and the smaller corals around it provide habitat for fish.

records.rights: Public domain image, The Met Open Access (CC0).

records.title: Twelve seconds at Kitty Hawk
records.summary: Orville Wright lies at the controls as the Flyer lifts off on 17 December 1903. Wilbur runs beside it. This first flight covered 120 feet in 12 seconds.
records.alt: The Wright Flyer just above a sandy field with Wilbur Wright to the side.
records.caption: Orville Wright lies at the controls as the Flyer lifts off on 17 December 1903. Wilbur runs beside it. This first flight covered 120 feet in 12 seconds.

records.rights: Public domain in the United States.

records.title: Gandhi picks up salt at Dandi
records.summary: On 6 April 1930, Gandhi gathered salt at Dandi in defiance of British salt law. This surviving slide pairs the scene with a written title.
records.alt: A black-and-white slide shows Gandhi bending to the ground beside the title Breaking the Salt Law at Dandi.
records.caption: On 6 April 1930, Gandhi gathered salt at Dandi in defiance of British salt law. This surviving slide pairs the scene with a written title.
records.photographer: Photographer unidentified. Slide scanned by Yann.
records.rights: Public domain in India as identified by the source. The 1930 published work is also public domain in the United States.
records.derivative: Resized to fit 1800 pixels and encoded as JPEG.

records.title: Mercury through Mariner 10
records.summary: Mariner 10 photographed Mercury in 1974. Along the boundary between daylight and darkness, shadows reveal the relief of the cratered surface.
records.alt: A narrow sunlit portion of Mercury shows overlapping impact craters.
records.caption: Mariner 10 photographed Mercury in 1974. Along the boundary between daylight and darkness, shadows reveal the relief of the cratered surface.
records.rights: NASA Photojournal image, credited to NASA/JPL. See JPL Image Use Policy.
records.derivative: Uncropped JPEG resized to fit 1600 pixels.

records.title: Mars from the Viking orbiters
records.summary: This color mosaic combines Viking Orbiter images. The bright northern polar cap, the Tharsis volcanoes and the long canyon system Valles Marineris are visible in one projected view.
records.alt: A rust-colored globe has a bright northern cap and a dark canyon system below center.
records.caption: This color mosaic combines Viking Orbiter images. The bright northern polar cap, the Tharsis volcanoes and the long canyon system Valles Marineris are visible in one projected view.
records.rights: NASA Photojournal image, credited to NASA/JPL/USGS. See JPL Image Use Policy.
records.derivative: Uncropped JPEG resized to fit 1600 pixels.

records.title: The Sun in extreme ultraviolet
records.summary: NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory imaged the Sun on September 10, 2025. The golden color represents ultraviolet intensity rather than the Sun's visible-light color.
records.alt: Detailed glowing yellow-gold solar disk with active regions and wisps of corona against black space.
records.caption: A view of the Sun in a 171-angstrom extreme-ultraviolet band. This instrument image is rendered in false color, allowing hot solar structures to be seen.
records.rights: NASA science image; generally not subject to U.S. copyright, subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines.
records.derivative: NASA false-color 171-angstrom scientific image; resized to maximum edge 1800 pixels and saved as quality-87 JPEG without additional color remapping. NASA source original is linked.

records.title: Antarctica in summer, from orbit
records.summary: NASA Aqua MODIS imagery acquired January 27, 2009 depicts the continent's ice, surrounding seas and clouds. Several orbital passes were combined to form this mosaic.
records.alt: Large ice-white Antarctic continent surrounded by dark southern ocean and pale swirling cloud systems.
records.caption: A satellite mosaic shows Antarctica during the continuous summer daylight. This is a composite of several overpasses, not a single camera exposure.
records.rights: NASA Earth Observatory imagery; generally not subject to U.S. copyright, subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines.
records.photographer: NASA Earth Observatory / MODIS Rapid Response Team, NASA GSFC
records.derivative: NASA MODIS composite of multiple orbital passes. Downsampled to maximum edge 1800 pixels and saved as quality-87 JPEG; original acquisition link retained.

records.title: Aurora over Earth's night side
records.summary: Photographed from the International Space Station on September 7, 2026, auroral light glows above Earth's limb. Atmospheric atoms and molecules radiate after excitation associated with the solar wind.
records.alt: Thin green and purple auroral arcs above the dark curve of Earth, with distant city lights visible.
records.caption: An ISS view of a green and purple aurora. NASA cropped the photograph, enhanced contrast and removed lens artifacts.
records.rights: NASA astronaut photograph; generally not subject to U.S. copyright, subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines.
records.photographer: NASA / Expedition 75 crew / ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility
records.derivative: NASA cropped image, enhanced contrast and removed lens artifacts; the NASA derivative is resized to maximum edge 1800 pixels and saved as quality-87 JPEG.
